api-answers:
&api-questions;
The nbfx Shell API is the product-facing contract of the generic JavaFX application shell: the window facade and pane/tab manager, pane roles and hosts, the chrome and branding contracts, the UI-ready hook, the window-environment capabilities, the shutdown contract and the pane-provider SPI, the window-system lifecycle and its WindowSink/WindowState model, plus CJAP declarative shell-region/profile metadata, provider/frame contracts and region-host lifecycle. The shell implementation is nbfx.platform.shell.
A product implements the chrome/branding/window-environment contracts or registers a WindowPaneProvider; nbfx.platform.shell composes them and publishes the running window as ShellWindow and WindowManager. The API knows no project, IDE or Java type; editor documents and project state are resolved by the contribution through its lookup.
Product-facing shell contracts, including Node-free CJAP region/profile metadata and window options. This API remains devel until the CJAP reference product and scenarios pass.
Shell shutdown coordination contracts. This API remains devel until the CJAP reference product and scenarios pass.
Shell pane-provider SPI. This API remains devel until the CJAP reference product and scenarios pass.
A product replaces the application name, title, icons and stylesheets with ShellBranding.
A product supplies top/bottom chrome with ShellChromeProvider.
A product registers a permanent pane with WindowPaneProvider and moves content through WindowManager using stable content and group ids.
A product adds a shutdown participant with ShutdownParticipant.
An @OnUiReady task reaches the window through ShellWindowProvider.
A product declares shell chrome slots with @ShellRegionRegistration and reads immutable metadata through ShellRegionRegistry.
A product contributes fresh per-shell Nodes with @ShellContributionRegistration; metadata discovery never constructs classes or Nodes.
A product supplies a ShellProvider/ShellFrame while the runtime owns region mounting, update and disposal through ShellRegionHost.
A product declares per-window chrome with @ShellProfileRegistration and reads immutable metadata through ShellProfileRegistry.
A product registers a ChromeProfilePolicyProvider; pure ShellProfileResolver selection combines explicit options, hints, policy and neutral defaults without global lookup or JavaFX window access.
PaneRoleTest covers the canonical roles and the product-role rules. The shell modules exercise the contracts in their unit tests and the AppShell conformance fixture. The API is under development until the MVP freeze, after which signature tests (sigtest) are enabled. CJAP region tests cover id/kind canonicalization, immutable specs, direct-folder discovery, profile filtering, malformed/duplicate isolation and generated layer equality. Contribution tests cover loader-free metadata discovery, strict attributes, profile filtering before construction, fresh per-shell instances and DOCK exclusion. Frame API tests cover profile ids, context validation and optional renderer disposal. Profile tests cover immutable allow-lists/policies/options, strict direct-folder discovery, malformed-entry isolation, generated layer equality and service discovery. Runtime tests cover neutral profile declarations and the intersection of region applicability with profile allow-lists, including reuse of neutral slots by product-defined profiles. Resolver tests cover explicit/hint/policy/neutral precedence, decoration overrides, unknown-id fallback, duplicate ids and missing neutral profiles. Policy-provider tests cover named selection, absent providers, duplicate matches and null results.
A JDK is required to compile; JavaFX is provided by the runtime.
org.netbeans.api.nbfx.shell, org.netbeans.api.nbfx.shell.shutdown and org.netbeans.spi.nbfx.shell are exported. The implementation packages of nbfx.platform.shell are not.
ShellWindowProvider, the chrome/branding providers, the window-environment capabilities, ShellProfileHint and WindowPaneProvider are resolved from the shell/content lookup. ChromeProfilePolicyProvider is an NBM service resolved by nbfx.platform.shell against the optional product's policy id; @OnUiReady is a named service under NbFx/UIReady.
The host module registers its implementations; this module only defines the contracts. @ServiceProvider(service = Processor.class) registers ShellRegionRegistrationProcessor, ShellContributionRegistrationProcessor and ShellProfileRegistrationProcessor at compile time.
@ShellRegionRegistration writes direct region metadata folders under NbFx/ShellRegions; @ShellProfileRegistration writes direct profile metadata folders under NbFx/ShellProfiles. Direct .instance children of a region may declare ShellContribution implementations; nested menu/action folders are not region, profile or contribution metadata.
ShellRegionRegistry and ShellProfileRegistry read direct metadata folders and return immutable snapshots. ShellContributionRegistry reads direct class-based .instance children through LayerInstances and never uses DataObject, DataNode or InstanceCookie. It performs no implicit filesystem or network access.
None.
Window and scene-graph operations run on the JavaFX Application Thread. The shutdown confirmation runs on that thread, while the selected cleanup runs off it. CJAP region ids, specs, profile/policy metadata, annotation processing, discovery and resolver selection are Node-free and stateless. Contribution construction creates fresh per-shell instances. Provider/frame creation and region mount/update/dispose run on the JavaFX Application Thread under the runtime mount owner's lifecycle.
No code runs on startup; the contracts are resolved when the shell starts.
No code runs on exit beyond the registered shutdown participants.
No special requirements.
